newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish FinMin says no row with Riksbank on ERM.
newsitem.headline: Swedish FinMin says no row with Riksbank on ERM.

text.p: Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Thursday there was no conflict between the finance ministry and Sweden's central bank on the issue of linking the crown to Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM).
"We have very close contacts with the Riksbank, and we are in accord on the matter," Asbrink told a finance seminar in Stockholm.
Asbrink also repeated the government's stance that pegging the Swedish crown in the EU's ERM was not on the cards.
"Linking the crown to ERM is not on the agenda," he said.
The finance minister also said Sweden's foreign debt was too big and should be reduced. A continued positive trend for exports would help reduce this debt, he said.
"Exports continue to do well. We have a surplus in the current account, which means we can reduce our foreign debt."
Asbrink added there was no great hurry to re-vamp the process of wage agreements between employers and unions.
The Riksbank said in its inflation report on Tuesday excessive wage increases were fuelling inflation.
"The new wage round will take place in 1997. The partners (on the labour market) can use the time until then to update the process of the wage round," Asbrink said.
